content:
nina: noticed a weird UX for the Go generator: when the iterator Next(ctx) is used and the SDK retries auth mid-handshake, cancelling the ctx doesn't abort the handshake. sample app hangs.

theo: sdk version? retry policy?

nina: go-sdk v0.14.0-beta, default auth retry (3 attempts). snippet: 
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
gen := client.Generator("gpt-open", opts...)
go func(){ time.Sleep(200*time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
for gen.Next(ctx) { fmt.Println(gen.Value().Text) }
gen.Close()
```

rachel: interesting. so auth refresh triggers a blocking network backoff and the handshake goroutine sits in the retry loop with a background ctx. Cancel on the iterator ctx doesn't reach it.

nina: right, repro on linux and mac. pprof shows multiple goroutines stuck in oauth.TokenSource's Retry loop.

theo: two fixes: (1) thread the passed ctx into the handshake/token refresh path so cancellations propagate; (2) make Close(ctx) accept a timeout to avoid indefinite waits. both break existing ctor signature though.

rachel: small DX ask: update quickstart to prefer explicit ctx at construction or show the callback variant which doesn't hang because the callback gets called with ctx that is cancelled.

ci-bot: created issue DE-2401: "go-sdk: generator handshake/auth retry ignores iterator context cancel" https://tracker/internal/DE-2401

theo: i'll prototype adding WithHandshakeCtx(ctx) option and a CloseWithContext(ctx) helper. test will simulate auth retry with a fake token source and ensure CloseWithContext returns quickly after cancel.

nina: thanks. can we also add a short migration note and a line in the SDK quickstart about cancellation best-practices? new users keep hitting this.

rachel: agreed. i'll add a small note in onboarding and the sample app.

nina: filed a tiny repro gist: https://gist.github.com/nina/gen-auth-cancel. thanks for the quick triage!
